"EMERALD MINE 9X" is in the last part of its run, with only a small slice of its tickets still unsold. Late in a run, a game is worth a look when prizes outlast tickets. Early on, the prize design matters most. Here, neither the tickets nor the top prizes are running out faster than the other.

Today's free summary of "EMERALD MINE 9X" ends here. Every number behind it is on this page.
5055.headline: Early stage or late

5057.body:
"EASY MONEY" has 414,674 prizes of $2 still unclaimed, which is its most common win. Just below the top prize is the $10,000 prize, with two left. The full count for every prize level is listed below.

The numbers for "EASY MONEY" are recalculated every morning, and this page changes with them.
5057.headline: Prize table details

5059.body:
About two-thirds of the tickets for "THE CASH WHEEL" are sold. The top prize count has held, with two of six still unclaimed. The number of tickets printed is fixed, so that is a plain good sign.

Today's free summary of "THE CASH WHEEL" ends here. Every number behind it is on this page.
5059.headline: Six months, no top prize claimed

5060.body:
"FIND THE 7S" is near the end of its run, with about a quarter of its tickets still unsold. Late in a run, a game is worth a look when prizes outlast tickets. Early on, the prize design matters most. Here, top prizes are going faster than tickets, which is not a good sign.

Tomorrow's count on "FIND THE 7S" will be a little different. The game sells every day, and this page keeps track.
5060.headline: How much has sold

5063.body:
"CA$H IN HAND" is down to two top prizes after a $2 million winner was claimed four days ago. The game started with four top prizes. Know that before you buy, because a change in top prizes changes the whole game.

The numbers for "CA$H IN HAND" are recalculated every morning, and this page changes with them.
5063.headline: Someone claimed a $2 million prize
